messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High KV cache growth + continuous-batching token cadence stalls observed in prod region eu-west-1. Spike at 2024-11-03T14:12:25Z. See metric: kv_cache_size per-host rising >10x baseline and streaming_token_gap > 500ms.

maya: seeing the same in dashboards.  p95 latency for streaming endpoints jumped from 120ms -> 1.4s. A lot of small requests queued into big batches then stall at partial flush.

liam: oncall taking. dumping recent logs now. quick ask: do we have a recent config diff for batching/kv thresholds?

devin: pushing the last deploy diff: `git rev a1f3c9` — main change was `continuous_batching.enabled = true` + `batch_target_tokens = 2048` + new kv prefetch tweak.

natalie: tl;dr customer impact: Some streaming sessions see token cadence stalls (tokens sent in bursts, then long silence). A few customers reported interactive lag; CS flagged 2 paying customers.

oncall-bot: @liam, you're now the primary oncall (handed off by @maya). Handoff notes: infra has elevated eviction churn, paging latencies.

liam: switching to mitigation plan. Step 1: reduce batch_target_tokens to 512 and force partial flush every 50ms. Step 2: increase kv eviction aggressiveness to cap growth. Step 3: if issues persist, toggle `continuous_batching.enabled=false` for the streaming fleet.

maya: I can roll the config to a small canary (2 hosts) in eu-west-1 for testing.

devin: patch ready: `configs/streaming/batching_hotfix.yaml` snippet:
```yaml
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  batch_target_tokens: 512
  partial_flush_ms: 50
kv_cache:
  eviction_threshold: 0.7
  max_size_mb: 2048
```

liam: canary go from maya now. watch kv_cache_size, streaming_token_gap, and enqueue_depth.

maya: canary deployed to host-34 and host-36. monitoring...

deploy-bot: deploy started `configs/streaming/batching_hotfix.yaml` -> eu-west-1/canary (2 hosts). CI checks passed.

maya: initial signs good on the canary: kv_cache growth slowed, streaming cadence smoothed out. p95 down to ~280ms on canary.

liam: roll to 10% of fleet over next 5m. If stable, ramp. Also notify CS to update impacted customers with ETA. @cs-ops please prepare one-line status.

cs-ops: prepping message. Will notify the two affected customers with short note: "We're mitigating an issue causing intermittent streaming lag; small rollout underway; will update in 30m."

liam: ramping to 40% now. Keep watch for eviction churn (errors: `kv: eviction loop exceeded threshold`) and 5xx increase.

devin: noticed a small repro: when a large prefix cache miss occurs and the batch target is high, KV page loader stalls while batch waits for partial flush timer — creates backpressure. The hotfix reduces the window.

maya: at 40% ramp metrics look stable. No increase in 5xx. Token gap p95 trending down cluster-wide.

liam: ramp to 100% over next 10m. If anything regresses, immediate rollback to previous config or toggle `continuous_batching.enabled=false`.

deploy-bot: rollout 100% started -> eu-west-1.

maya: rollout complete. Post-rollout dashboards show kv_cache_size plateauing and streaming_token_gap normalized near baseline.

liam: summary: root cause appears to be interplay between aggressive `batch_target_tokens` and kv page load latencies causing partial flush stalls and unbounded cache growth. Hotfix reduced batch window and increased eviction aggressiveness.

natalie: customer impact: two customers reported degraded interactive streaming; both on eu-west-1, intermittent. CS notified and will follow up.

liam: next steps: 1) postmortem scheduled 2024-11-04 10:00 UTC, assign owners for batching config, kv prefetch logic, and monitoring gaps; 2) add guardrail alert: if kv_cache_size growth rate > 3x baseline in 5m, auto-toggle batching to safe config; 3) run load test to reproduce large-prefix miss + high batch_target scenario.

devin: I'll open an RFC for safer batching defaults + an automated canary verifier for streaming cadence.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: SEV-2 -> resolution: mitigation deployed and validated; follow-up actions scheduled.

liam: thanks everyone. I'm leaving a short note in the oncall handoff doc and tagging owners. Closing thread once postmortem scheduled is added. :thumbsup:
